newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Big SPX put order is the feature.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Big SPX put order is the feature.

text.p: A roughly 20,000 contract put order was the highlight of trading in major U.S. index options Wednesday, traders said.
In S&P 500 index .SPX options, the July 815 put traded nearly 10,800 contracts and the September 750 put traded roughly 10,750 by early afternoon.
Most of the volume in both contracts was done in large blocks.
"That's where the action was," one S&P 100 index options dealer said. "It was a big portfolio hedge."
Traders said the order was put in by a Wall Street brokerage.
At about 1240 CDT/1740 GMT, the SPX was up about half a point at 896.90 and the OEX was down about half a point at around 875.
Trading overall in SPX options was fairly heavy.
"We've had a couple of big call sellers," one SPX options trader said. "They were pounding some put premium today too."
Busy SPX calls included the July 910s, which traded 9,300 contracts, the July 935s, which traded 5,145 and the July 830s, which traded 2,900.
The SPX trader said some of the July 935 call activity was a brokerage buying them as part of a spread involving the July 900 series.
Among other active SPX puts, the July 835 traded 7,360, the July 900s traded 7,200 and the July 845s traded 6,135.
Jack Callahan, an independent market maker in OEX options, said trading in that pit was steady.
OEX activity was led by the July 850 put, which traded 3,715 contracts and the July 860 put, which traded 2,790.
Overall, OEX puts outpaced calls by 21,330 to 19,660 in early afternoon activity.
In the SPX, put volume led call volume by 59,818 to 28,690.

Jerry Hegarty, an options analyst at Thomson Financial Services, said in a midday report that the market's down opening followed by a lower first hour and then a recovery suggested a possible solid upside move late in the day.
"These types of days are usually very strong at the end of the day," he said.
